name: Amoebic keratitis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and microbiological diagnostic criteria for amoebic keratitis

criteria.description: Presence of severe ocular pain disproportionate to clinical signs
Characteristic ring-shaped corneal stromal infiltrates on slit-lamp examination
Detection of Acanthamoeba cysts or trophozoites by corneal scraping microscopy or culture
In vivo confocal microscopy showing double-walled cysts in corneal stroma
Poor response to antibacterial and antifungal therapy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic clinical signs (severe pain and ring-shaped stromal infiltrates) plus microbiological confirmation of Acanthamoeba
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Early diagnosis is critical to prevent vision loss; confocal microscopy is a useful adjunct.

common.symptomName: Abnormality of the posterior segment of the globe

laboratory: Microscopic identification of Acanthamoeba cysts or trophozoites in corneal scrapings
Culture of Acanthamoeba on non-nutrient agar with E. coli overlay
PCR detection of Acanthamoeba DNA from corneal samples
imaging: In vivo confocal microscopy revealing double-walled cysts in corneal stroma
Slit-lamp biomicroscopy showing ring-shaped stromal infiltrates and perineural infiltrates
other: Poor response to antibacterial and antifungal treatments
History of contact lens use or corneal trauma

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of dendritic ulcers on corneal epithelium
Positive PCR for herpes simplex virus
Usually less severe pain compared to amoebic keratitis

redFlags: Severe ocular pain disproportionate to clinical signs
Rapid progression to corneal perforation if untreated
references: Dart JK, Saw VP, Kilvington S. Acanthamoeba keratitis: diagnosis and treatment update 2009. Am J Ophthalmol. 2009;148(4):487-499.
Tu EY. Acanthamoeba Keratitis: Diagnosis and Treatment Update 2015. Am J Ophthalmol. 2015;160(4):484-489.
